versions.changelog:
Version 0.0.1 — first release published through the new distribution system

This is a pre-release build for bench testing. Version numbers stay in the
0.0.x range until the firmware is meant for general use, at which point it
becomes 1.0.0.

The update mechanism itself changed: releases are now published per platform
with the firmware image served as a release asset, and the board verifies the
package's SHA-256 against the manifest before it swaps boot partitions. Large
updates transfer in resumable chunks, so a dropped connection costs one chunk
rather than the whole download.

Streaming receive
- E1.31 preview-flagged packets no longer drive live output, and a sender that
  terminates its stream releases the outputs immediately instead of holding the
  last frame until the silence timeout expires.
- DDP: the all-devices destination id is accepted, storage-flagged packets are
  no longer displayed, unsupported pixel formats are refused rather than
  painted as garbage, and RGBW payloads pass through untouched so RGBW strips
  render correctly.
- Universe layouts honour a configurable channels-per-universe, so xLights'
  510-channel universes land on the channels the sequence expects.
- Optional per-sender arbitration: the highest-priority source owns a universe
  until it goes quiet, matching FPP's behaviour.

Effects, looks and routines
- Saved effects and layer stacks are now one concept, a Look: a saved
  composition of one or more layers.
- Looks arranged over time are an Effect Routine, edited on a sequential
  timeline where order is time. Transitions between steps render as real
  cross-fades.
- "Sequence" now means an FSEQ frame file, matching what xLights and FPP mean
  by the word.

Diagnostics
- The device log is now populated and readable from the web UI, so a
  misbehaving board can be diagnosed from a log bundle instead of a serial
  cable. The log view says so when the log it is showing is incomplete.

Scheduling and sensors
- Sunrise and sunset use the full NOAA solar algorithm. This fixes locations
  east of roughly +90 degrees longitude, which previously fell back to a fixed
  06:00/18:00 schedule year round.
- Sensor calibration accepts a two-point scale-and-offset model, with a
  reference-value solve for single-point correction.

Fleet
- A live fleet page with per-board health, delivery reporting, and update
  status across every board on the network.

Pixel output
- An output with no streaming channel assignment is no longer blanked every
  frame; new outputs are created with a usable channel assignment by default.
- A source that stops writing stops owning the pixels, so a stalled sender can
  no longer lock out effects or playback until reboot.
